inspection_scope: Complete data-only review of the supplied film plan, including its sole chapter, setup, beat contract, semantic center, planned hierarchy, before/after state, narration coverage, and token lifecycle.

checks.evidence: The plan contains one physical card setup and does not ask that world to explain multiple unrelated mechanisms or physical rules.
No mechanisms or states accumulate across the single beat; the card, Bot, and basic set remain static.
Only one intended hero group—the answer card—is planned, with the Bot and caption beside it; there are not multiple unrelated dominant object groups.
There is only one setup and one proposition, so no sequence of unrelated propositions repeats the same composition.
The setup and film-level continuity-token lists are empty, so no persistent tokens obscure the argument.

The paper backboard, work surface, card supports, Bot, and corner crop each have an identified setting, support, participant, or attention-directing function; the plan does not establish purposeless decorative geometry.
The complete argument occupies one short proposition and one setup. No semantic shift occurs that would require an internal reset.

In s1, the intended focal target is the blank answer card, but its dominant action is only decorative floating with no state change. The composition simultaneously assigns a large caption the entire conclusion and places a Bot beside the card. Because the card performs no testing, comparison, or selection, the planned primary action cannot command the glance over the meaning-bearing caption.

In s1/b1, the narration claims that tested answers should win, while the before and after states explicitly leave the same blank card unchanged. The contract states that no test, comparison, or selection is visible and that captions alone say an answer was tested and selected.

setup_assessments.evidence: The setup covers the full narration span, but its central action does not enact its semantic center, “Select after testing.” Its unchanged before/after state leaves the large caption to communicate both testing and winning, preventing the planned card action from functioning as the dominant focus.

violations.observation: The blank card is named as the hero and focal target but remains unchanged and floats decoratively, while a large caption contains the entire conclusion and a small Bot supplies another figure. The meaning-bearing caption therefore competes with and functionally supersedes the nominal primary action.
violations.smallest_structural_correction: Make the card stage the single dominant causal sequence: visibly undergo a test, receive a result, and move into a selected/winner position. Keep the Bot only if it performs or reacts to that sequence, and reduce the caption to editorial context rather than the dominant explanation.

violations.observation: The shot contract explicitly provides no visible test, comparison, selection, or change between entry and exit; captions alone supply every essential claim in the sentence.
violations.smallest_structural_correction: Replace the static illustration with a visible condition-to-result progression inside s1: present at least one answer candidate, visibly test it, then show the passing candidate selected or advanced as the consequence. The caption may echo “tested” or “wins,” but must not supply the missing causality.

limits: This data-only review evaluates planned structure and hierarchy from the supplied contracts. It cannot establish rendered readability, pixel-level visibility, actual mobile-glance performance, animation execution, or listening experience.
